guard: the AG-UI event grant names the principal the manager allocated, is minted only when the launch armed the plane, and is carried forward, arming included, by the record a restart reads
why: The failure this guard exists for is quiet in every direction that matters. A grant keyed on the
display name is a well-formed subject that parses back to a well-formed principal, so nothing
downstream rejects it; it simply authorizes two agents onto one stream the first time the manager
auto-numbers a collision. A grant minted unconditionally looks identical to a correct one on any
agent that did arm. And a record that carries the channel but drops the arming flag brings a
session back holding publish rights it will never use, which reads as a working system with an
empty panel.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports the manager by relative source path (../src/manager.js), so
the bytes mutated are the bytes graded: no dist in the path, no build in the command. Its
package-name imports are core's own vocabulary (eventChannel, principalKey, DEV_OWNER), which is
the point of two cells here, and is not what any mutation below touches.
NOT PROVED HERE, named rather than implied. The suite reads the preservation inventory; it does
not run the resume rail. That is deliberate and it is a real limit: a resume ADOPTS the
credential the spawn wrote and refuses when the adopted authority stops matching the inventory,
so what a restart can lose is the record, which is what these cells read. A defect in the resume
rail's own re-launch would not be caught here.
The last mutation is about an upgrade rather than a spawn: a strict schema is the correct instinct
everywhere except on a document the previous version wrote, where it converts a restart into a loss.
The read side is asserted from the decoded credential rather than from the design, because the
question a plane carrying full tool inputs and outputs raises is who may SUBSCRIBE to it. Arming
grants publish on one channel and adds nothing to what the agent may read, not even its own
plane. What a credential admits on the read side is exactly what the agent's access set names,
so a persona file that names a foreign event channel would grant that read: that is local
operator capability, and it is not reachable from any peer-facing tool.

mutations.name: G1 key the grant on the display name, the mistake the whole derivation exists to prevent
mutations.find: if (events) allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })];
mutations.replace: if (events) allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: name })];
mutations.expectRed: the display name does NOT appear in the granted channel
mutations.cell: the display name does NOT appear in the granted channel
mutations.note: The name is in scope at this line and reads as the obvious identifier, which is exactly why this is the authoring error to fence. Every other positive cell about the channel would still pass a prefix or round-trip test on the result.

mutations.name: G2 mint the grant for every spawn, armed or not
mutations.find: if (events) allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })];
mutations.replace: allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })];
mutations.expectRed: no event channel is granted when events are off
mutations.cell: no event channel is granted when events are off
mutations.note: An unconditional grant satisfies every cell about the armed agent. Only the unarmed sibling sees it.

mutations.name: G3 no grant at all
mutations.find: if (events) allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })];
mutations.expectRed: exactly one event channel is granted
mutations.cell: exactly one event channel is granted

mutations.name: G4 the restart record keeps the channel but drops the arming
mutations.expectRed: the inventory carries the arming flag, not just the grant
mutations.cell: the inventory carries the arming flag, not just the grant
mutations.note: The half of a restart that leaves no visible damage: the resumed session still holds the grant, connects fine, and publishes nothing.

mutations.name: G5 the refusal keeps the reserved name
mutations.find:
this.reserved.delete(name);
      return { ok: false, error: `connector "${connector.name}" does not publish an AG-UI event plane
mutations.replace: return { ok: false, error: `connector "${connector.name}" does not publish an AG-UI event plane
mutations.expectRed: the refusal releases the reserved name
mutations.cell: the refusal releases the reserved name
mutations.note: A leaked reserve is silent: the next spawn of that persona is auto-numbered and nothing says why.

mutations.name: G6 require the arming flag in the resume document, refusing every inventory the previous version wrote
mutations.expectRed: an inventory written before the event plane still parses
mutations.cell: an inventory written before the event plane still parses
mutations.note: The upgrade hazard: a manager restarted onto a new binary reads an inventory the old one wrote, and a required field turns that restart into a loss of every agent it was preserving.

mutations.name: G7 arming grants the channel on the READ side too, so an armed agent can subscribe to a plane
mutations.find: if (events) allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })];
mutations.replace: if (events) { allowPublish = [...(allowPublish ?? []), connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })]; allowSubscribe = [...allowSubscribe, connector.eventChannel!({ owner: agentTriple.owner, actor: agentTriple.actor })]; }
mutations.expectRed: arming grants no event channel on the READ side
mutations.cell: arming grants no event channel on the READ side
mutations.note: The symmetric-looking edit a later reader could make while 'tidying up', and the one that turns arming into a read capability. An event channel carries a session's full tool inputs and outputs, so what a credential ADMITS matters more than what it may write.
